title: Browse, pick, develop: the catalog
objective: Deliver a two-step flow: browse cards and folders very fast through an automatic organization into events, days, cameras and moments, examine frames in detail and pick a few; develop only the picks into catalog folders, browsed in Select and edited in Develop through a development-set filmstrip, with every long job visible and every operation in the one command registry.
context_summary: Planning proposal, not implementation authorization: eighteen proposals await the owner (the first task). The work is divided into one contracts task and four parallel lanes, as the design's delivery plan sets out: A files (metadata, index, watchers, events and moments), B previews (lane and cache, bracket-from-previews, 100% region, rendered previews), C catalog (picks and journal, folders and collections, developing picks, removal, batch, availability, Locate, resolving missing originals) and D views and desktop (browse views, the Select workspace, loupe, the Develop confirmation and filmstrip, catalog browsing, missing-originals UI, long-running work). At most four implementers run at once, each owning its lane's modules; lane D starts on the contracts' generated data. Suggested order per implementer once the contracts (TASK-002) land: A — TASK-003, 004, 006, 005; B — TASK-007, 009, 010, then 008 once 006 lands; C — TASK-011, 012, 013, 016, 017, 014, 015; D — TASK-018 once 006 lands, then 019, 024, 020, 021, 022, 023. The integrator lands TASK-002 first and runs TASK-025 last. Today the catalog imports one file at a time by fully decoding and developing it on the one source worker, persists no capture metadata, stores no previews and exposes only a paged `catalog.list`; the desktop holds one document and never lists photographs. Timing runs wait for the last task.

tasks.description: Resolve the catalog proposals and authorize implementation.
extra_context: The design is a proposal with eighteen numbered defaults (P1 to P18). P1 (browse, pick, develop), P2 (no ratings or keywords), P15 (catalog folders from events), P17 (keeping the index current) and P18 (showing long-running work) follow the owner's own direction. Planning does not authorize implementation (AGENTS.md, How we work).
HDR and panorama merging stay unselected; the design only leaves room for a merge source kind. Backup, portability, sidecars and sync stay open storage questions.
acceptance_criteria: Each of P1 to P18 is accepted, changed or deferred and recorded in docs/decisions.md and the design.
Implementation is explicitly authorized, or the plan stays a proposal.
Changed defaults are reflected in the design and in the affected tasks before they start.

steps: Walk the owner through the boards and the proposals table.
Record each answer with its date.
expected_results: Every proposal has an owner answer recorded; the pending tasks match it.

tasks.description: Land the contracts every lane codes against: catalog format 12 and the index schema, the shared types module, declared method shapes, generated data at the design scale, and module skeletons with per-lane sections in the hot shared files.
extra_context: Done by the integrator (or one implementer, reviewed by the integrator) before any lane starts; it creates the integration branch the lanes start from.

Format 11 is `CATALOG_FORMAT` in crates/luxforge-core/src/editor/catalog.rs, created by `EditorService::create_schema` and checked on open in editor.rs; format 11 is refused by name and never rewritten. The index database is separate (`<catalog>.index/index.sqlite`), versioned, and discarded on a mismatch without touching the catalog.
Methods are registered by the lane that implements them, when they work, so `schema.list` never lists a stub; this task declares their shapes in the types module and the design's API table only.

The generator writes indexes (10,000 files across trips with GPS, bursts, brackets with and without exposure bias, undated files) and catalogs (100,000 and 1,000,000 photographs with picks, catalog folders, collections and missing originals) with no image files, and small image folders whose files carry real embedded thumbnails, for the preview and desktop lanes.

acceptance_criteria: An empty database initializes as format 12 with every table, index and constraint the design lists; format 11 and earlier are refused by name without changing their bytes; the index database is created, versioned and discarded independently.

The shared types (identities, header metadata, events and moments, view queries and rows, picks, library changes, job progress) exist in one core module with serde shapes matching the design's API table.
`cargo xtask generate-catalog --files N --assets M --output NEW` and its image-folder mode are deterministic from a seed.

Skeleton modules exist for `core/src/index`, `organize`, `previews`, `library` and `browse` and the desktop's `select` state, view and app files, and the hot shared files carry one marked section per lane.
versions-and-lineage.md describes format 12; the architecture lists the new modules and the index directory.

Generate and open the large catalogs and the image folders.

tasks.description: Lane A: Read typed header metadata from a bounded header read, including subsecond time, offset, body serial, exposure bias and GPS.
extra_context: `CaptureMetadata` (crates/luxforge-core/src/export/metadata/mod.rs, reader in read.rs) parses a 33-field EXIF whitelist from JPEG and TIFF-structured or RAF-embedded RAW, but its values are private and it is built only from a whole prepared source. CR3 keeps its metadata in ISO-BMFF boxes and needs its own bounded path.
Produces the contracts' header-metadata type for lanes A (organize), C (developing) and D (Info panel). The export's written field set must not change.

context_links.label: Catalog design
context_links.relevance: Lanes, ownership, contracts and integration rules.

acceptance_criteria: Typed values (capture time with subsecond and offset, make, model, body serial, lens, exposure time, f-number, ISO, exposure bias, focal lengths, GPS, dimensions, orientation, the embedded thumbnail's location) come from a header read bounded in bytes.
Values equal those read from the whole file for every fixture and one authentic file of each RAW format the camera catalog admits; export output is byte-identical before and after.

steps: Accessor tests including missing, malformed and offset-less times.
Export metadata tests unchanged.
expected_results: Header metadata is typed, bounded and cheap.

tasks.description: Lane A: Build the index lane: listing and header reads for cards and folders, reconciliation by signature, exclusions, offline folders and progress on the activity board.
extra_context: Two workers on different files write the index database; the catalog owner is not involved. No hashing and no image data beyond the embedded thumbnail's bytes when they sit in the header read.

Exclusions: macOS packages (such as a Photos library), other applications' caches (such as Lightroom `.lrdata`), hidden and system folders, and Luxforge's own catalog and index directories. Progress uses the activity board's shared `ActivityProgress` with an honest count while a walk is still discovering its extent.
Produces `index.refresh` and the index rows that lanes B and D read.

context_links.label: Performance rules
context_links.relevance: Owner-thread, bounded-queue and idle rules; the review checklist.

acceptance_criteria: Indexing a generated mixed folder lists every supported file with header metadata, follows no symlink out of its roots, crosses no volume, skips every excluded kind and refuses past its file limit with `resource-limit`.
Reconciliation keeps unchanged rows, re-reads changed ones, adds new and drops vanished files, and carries rows across a move within a volume by file identity.
Files are unchanged by hash, length, time and location; deleting the index directory while closed rebuilds the same content.
Every run is on the activity board with progress and cancels through `job.cancel`.

steps: Core tests over generated folders, a disk image for offline and removable cases, and injected unreadable files.
expected_results: Browsing is cheap, bounded, read-only, visible and disposable.

tasks.description: Lane A: Watch indexed folders with the platform's change notifications and reconcile cards on mount and network volumes on open.
extra_context: FSEvents on macOS, including replay of what changed while Luxforge was closed; the change journal or directory notifications on Windows; inotify on Linux; through one pinned dependency or thin per-platform code, recorded in the dependency policy. Mount notifications (Disk Arbitration on macOS) trigger card reconciliation and `card.list` updates. No polling (performance rule 8).
Windows and Linux are implemented and unit-tested where the notification API allows; native checks there stay deferred with the rest of the platform work.

context_links.label: Catalog design
context_links.relevance: Lanes, ownership, contracts and integration rules.

context_links.label: Performance rules

acceptance_criteria: A file added, changed, renamed or removed in an indexed folder updates the index without a rescan; changes made while Luxforge was closed are caught up on open on macOS.
Mounting a card lists it under `card.list` and reconciles it; unmounting marks its rows offline.
An idle catalog with watchers armed uses no CPU beyond the notifications themselves (checked with the existing idle measurement once in the final task).

steps: Core tests driving a temporary folder and a disk image.
expected_results: The index keeps up with the disk without polling.

tasks.description: Lane A: Organize files into events by time and place and into days, cameras and moments from metadata (bursts by speed, brackets by exposure metadata), with the bundled gazetteer.
extra_context: Pure functions of ordered header metadata, the gazetteer and view thresholds (P3, P5); nothing is stored. The preview-brightness bracket check is lane B's and plugs in through a declared classifier input.
The gazetteer is a bundled data asset (for example GeoNames cities15000, CC BY 4.0) with its notice; the manual asset review stays deferred. Nearest-place lookup by a k-d tree or grid, no network.
A labelled corpus is needed (trips with positions, bursts, brackets with and without bias, single frames, several makes), gathered as the RAW corpus was; the generated data covers the unit tests.

context_links.label: Catalog design
context_links.relevance: Lanes, ownership, contracts and integration rules.

acceptance_criteria: Events and moments on generated data equal an independent grouping; the corpus evaluation and chosen thresholds are recorded in the design.

Event names follow the design's order (place, user-named folder, date and cameras) without any network request; undated files form an Undated event per folder; changing a threshold regroups without touching stored data.

steps: Property tests of the grouping functions.
A corpus evaluation run recorded once.
expected_results: Events and moments match how the photographs were taken.

tasks.description: Lane B: Build the preview lane and cache: embedded preview extraction per camera, grid and loupe tiers, priority by look-ahead and visibility, and progress.
extra_context: Nothing stores previews today; the proxy (proxy.rs) is one in-memory entry in the preview worker. The lane never uses or evicts the editor's one-slot `source_cache`.

Embedded previews through `luxforge-raw` (LibRaw), scaled JPEG decodes through `luxforge-jpeg`; files keyed by signature from the contracts' identity type, so the lane starts on the generated image folders before the index lane lands; loupe tier in the shared LRU budget (P8).
Record for every camera in the corpus the sizes of its embedded thumbnail and largest preview, and which carry no usable preview; that inventory decides where the development fallback runs.

context_links.label: Catalog design
context_links.relevance: Lanes, ownership, contracts and integration rules.

acceptance_criteria: `preview.read` returns a cached preview with what it is, or a job; the look-ahead outranks visible cells, which outrank the rest; the grid can draw from the embedded thumbnail before the larger preview arrives.
The loupe tier respects its byte budget; the per-camera inventory is recorded in the design.
The lane reports progress on the activity board and cancels through `job.cancel`.

steps: Cache key, priority, budget and eviction tests over the generated image folders.
expected_results: Previews arrive in the order you look at them, labelled.

tasks.description: Lane B: Classify brackets from previews when metadata cannot say, from the embedded thumbnails' brightness with framing checked.
extra_context: Mean log luminance of a small centre-weighted thumbnail per frame and an edge correlation to confirm unchanged framing; a consistent step of about two thirds of a stop or more makes a bracket labelled `from previews` with the measured steps (P5). Plugs into lane A's organize functions through their declared classifier input.

context_links.label: Catalog design
context_links.relevance: Lanes, ownership, contracts and integration rules.

acceptance_criteria: On generated thumbnails with known exposure steps and on the labelled corpus's metadata-less brackets, classification and measured steps agree within the recorded tolerance; bursts with changing light are not called brackets.
A run costs under a millisecond on decoded thumbnails.

steps: Synthetic step and false-positive tests.
Corpus evaluation recorded once.
expected_results: Brackets are found even when the camera does not say.

tasks.description: Lane B: Add the 100% region decode and the on-demand development fallback for cameras whose preview is smaller than the sensor.
extra_context: `preview.region` decodes only the rows and columns it needs of a full-size embedded preview (libjpeg-turbo's cropped and scaled decode); otherwise it develops that frame neutrally, one RAW at a time, off the editor's cache, labelled as a Luxforge development (P6).

context_links.label: Catalog design
context_links.relevance: Lanes, ownership, contracts and integration rules.

acceptance_criteria: A region of a full-size preview is decoded without decoding the whole preview; the fallback develops at most one RAW at a time and labels its result.
Neither path touches the editor's source cache.

steps: Region-bounds and allocation tests.
Fallback labelling and concurrency tests.
expected_results: Focus can be checked on any frame.

extra_context: Rendered through the proxy path at thumbnail size, so approximations of the entry at that size; a commit makes a new key and the old file is collected; a renderer generation change discards rendered tiers. Until the first render a RAW shows its camera preview, marked as such.

tasks.description: Lane C: Add picks and the library journal with undo and redo.
extra_context: Every mutation carries `{request_id, actor}` and is deduplicated. A pick is kept by path and signature until developed or cleared. One library change is one journal row plus per-item before/after rows, at most `MAX_LIBRARY_BATCH` items, and one event naming its sequence (the event log holds 256). Undo appends the inverse, only for the calling client's own changes, and refuses on an intervening change. No ratings, keywords or flags (P2).
Produces the journal every other lane C task and lane D's undo use.

context_links.label: Catalog design
context_links.relevance: Lanes, ownership, contracts and integration rules.

acceptance_criteria: `pick.set` and `pick.list` work over paths, ids or the selection; picks survive a restart.
Undo and redo restore exact prior values, refuse on intervening changes naming the items, and are journaled; a 5,000-item change records one event; `library.journal` pages after a cursor.

steps: Journal and undo tests with two concurrent clients.
Batch-limit refusal.
Restart persistence.
expected_results: Every pick is attributed, durable, bounded and undoable.

tasks.description: Lane C: Add catalog folders (create, rename, nest, merge, delete, move photographs) and collections, groups and smart collections.
extra_context: Every developed photograph is in exactly one catalog folder (P15); year grouping is a view concern. A smart collection stores a browse query and may not refer to another. Every change is a library change; nothing on disk changes.

context_links.label: Catalog design
context_links.relevance: Lanes, ownership, contracts and integration rules.

acceptance_criteria: `folder.*` and `asset.move` are journaled and undoable; deleting a folder that holds photographs is refused.
`collection.*` creates, renames, moves, deletes and changes membership, journaled; a reference to a smart collection is refused.

steps: Folder tree, merge and move tests; collection membership and smart-query validation.
expected_results: The catalog can be organized the way the person wants.

tasks.description: Lane C: Develop picks into the catalog on the develop lane, into the chosen catalog folder per event, with linking, relinking, card-copy substitution, removable-media confirmation and sending back; replace `catalog.import`.
extra_context: Today `catalog.import` fully decodes and develops a file on the one source worker (capacity 8) before committing (`import_prepared`, editor/source.rs), and `job.adopt` accepts only the client's latest import. The develop lane streams the fingerprint and reads the RAW interpretation without developing, off the source worker; whether any format needs its mosaic unpacked is measured and recorded.

`pick.plan` proposes each event's folder (new, named after the event, or the one an earlier Develop from the same event span made). An identical file links; a missing original relinks through `EditorService::relocate` only on a fingerprint match; card picks use verified copies from indexed folders (P8); sending back deletes a photograph with only its Original entry (P9). A single opened file is picked and developed at once. Records each photograph's `source_folder`.

context_links.label: Catalog design
context_links.relevance: Lanes, ownership, contracts and integration rules.

acceptance_criteria: `pick.develop` creates exactly the picked photographs with fingerprints, interpretations, Original entries, capture metadata and source folders, in the folders `into` names, in batches, clearing committed picks; cancellation or a failing file keeps every committed photograph whole and nothing partial; a retry answers with the first result; progress is on the activity board.

Identical files link, missing originals relink only on a match, card picks use verified copies when asked, removable media otherwise needs `confirm_removable`, and `asset.send-back` refuses a photograph with history beyond its Original.
`catalog.import` and `catalog.list` are removed; opening a photograph uses `source.prepare` with a generalized adopt; originals are unchanged by hash, length, time and location.

steps: Core tests over generated folders with every case, cancellation mid-batch and injected failures.
An API conformance test through `luxforge-json`.
expected_results: Only picks enter the catalog, into their folders, off the editor's path.

tasks.description: Lane C: Add Remove from catalog, Removed, Put back and Empty Removed.
extra_context: Removal is a journaled library change. Emptying deletes catalog records including immutable history, so it lifts the immutability triggers only inside its own transaction and needs permission authority (P12).

context_links.label: Catalog design
context_links.relevance: Lanes, ownership, contracts and integration rules.

acceptance_criteria: Removed photographs leave every other view and return intact with Put back; files are untouched.
`catalog.empty-removed` is refused to an edit-authority client and otherwise deletes only removed photographs, collecting their unreferenced strokes and artifacts; no other path deletes an entry.

steps: Removal, restore, authority and collection tests.
expected_results: Removing is reversible; erasing history needs the person.

extra_context: Each photograph is its own history entry or export; skips (an open draft, a historical preview in the session, a missing original) are reported with reasons. Batch export uses the existing JPEG export and naming rule only (P11).

tasks.description: Lane C: Track original availability by volume and ship manual Locate through the API.
extra_context: The internal relocation write exists (`EditorService::relocate`, crate-visible, test-only access through `OwnerMessage::Relocate`); Locate verifies the fingerprint first on a bounded, cancellable job. Availability is persisted with its check time; an absent mount point marks a volume's photographs offline with one check; a file moved within its volume is found again by identity and confirmed by fingerprint.

context_links.relevance: Lanes, ownership, contracts and integration rules.

acceptance_criteria: Every item of the source-recovery spec's Locate acceptance passes through the API.
An unmounted disk image marks its photographs offline; Develop and export refuse with the reason; a same-volume move is recovered by identity after a fingerprint check.

steps: Core tests with a mounted disk image and copied fixtures, never the user's archive.
expected_results: Missing originals are known and recoverable one at a time.

tasks.description: Lane C: Resolve missing originals per photograph, grouped by the folder on disk each was developed from.
extra_context: Gated on P11. `source.missing` groups by `source_folder` with reasons; `source.find` searches one chosen folder by name and size, then fingerprint, with a result per photograph (found, different bytes, several identical candidates, not found, already claimed); `source.relink` commits verified pairs in one transaction as one undoable library change and updates each `source_folder`.

context_links.label: Catalog design
context_links.relevance: Lanes, ownership, contracts and integration rules.

acceptance_criteria: Results are correct for moved, rewritten, duplicated and deleted files; a file another photograph points at is never taken; identical candidates wait for a choice.
Stop, failure or an unplugged volume leaves everything as it was; the search shows progress and cancels.

steps: Core tests with moved, rewritten, duplicated and missing files.
expected_results: Moved originals are found and relinked per photograph, verified.

tasks.description: Lane D: Add owner-held browse views, facets and selection over events, folders on disk, cards and the catalog.
extra_context: A view is the client's one ordered item list with day, camera and moment boundaries in its `ClientSession` (api/mod.rs), 16 bytes an item, marked stale by library-change and index revisions. Queries are structured JSON, never SQL text. Grouping calls lane A's organize functions. Works on the contracts' generated data before lanes A and C land their writers. P13 decides the fallback if the measurement misses.

context_links.label: Catalog design
context_links.relevance: Lanes, ownership, contracts and integration rules.

acceptance_criteria: Views and group boundaries agree with an independent evaluation over generated indexes and catalogs, including picks, moments, catalog folders, missing capture times, removed photographs and every sort's tie-break.

Facet counts equal the views they predict; `browse.rows` reads windows by position; `browse.select` supports replace, add, remove, ranges and all-in-view and is reported in `session.state`; `event.list` searches by place, date and camera.

steps: Agreement tests on seeded data.
Session selection and staleness tests.
expected_results: One query model answers every view in Select.

tasks.description: Lane D: Build the Select workspace: workspace switch, sources (search, cards, events, on disk, catalog with folders by year), the grouped virtualized grid, the Info panel, picking and Develop N's button.

Built against generated data from the contracts; switches to each lane's real methods as they land. The grid creates each image handle once and keeps it while the cell is shown, with decoded previews under a byte budget. Every gesture sends the request its API equivalent sends. `P` is a journaled change; `Cmd+Z` undoes this client's last; an agent's pick appears without a reload.
